cl_lsd_nbome.q: What are NBOMes, and are they sold as LSD?
cl_lsd_nbome.short: Yes, sometimes. NBOMes are lab-made drugs, mostly sold on blotters. In case reports up to 2014, several people who got sick or died thought they'd taken LSD.
cl_lsd_nbome.but: Nobody has counted how often 'LSD' blotters hold NBOMes. And these are reports of people who got sick, so they can't say how risky one use is.
how: NBOMes are lab-made relatives of the 2C drugs. Of the first 10 found in Europe, from 2011 to 2013, 8 were on blotters. In some cases, blotters taken as 'acid' turned out to hold an NBOMe.
In 29 published cases of poisoning, nearly all had a racing heart and about 4 in 10 had seizures. Some needed intensive care, a breathing machine or dialysis.
Published cases are often the worst ones. Of 25 cases reported to Texas poison centres, 4 in 100 had seizures, against about 38 in 100 published cases.
By 2014, eight deaths had been reported with 25I-NBOMe, and a lab found it in five. Some had taken other drugs too. The review says its role in the deaths was often unclear.
cl_lsd_nbome.rate: One review of case reports up to 2014. Case reports pick out people who got very sick, only about half had the drug found in their own samples, and nobody counted everyone who used NBOMes.

cl_benzo_designer.q: Are designer benzos like etizolam more dangerous?
cl_benzo_designer.short: Nobody has tested that. Of 141 deaths with a designer benzo in published reports, 115 also listed an opioid, and only 3 listed no other drug.
cl_benzo_designer.but: These reports only count people who got into trouble, not everyone who used. So they can't say how risky one use is.
how: US poison centres, 2014 to 2017: in 234 reports naming a designer benzo and no other drug, mostly etizolam, 65 in 100 people were drowsy and 3 in 100 needed a breathing tube. One man died.
Nobody lab-tested which drug these people took. Reports rose from 26 to 112 a year, partly because new drugs got their own codes in 2016.

A review of published cases to 2021 found 141 death entries, mostly phenazepam, flualprazolam and etizolam. 115 also listed an opioid, and only 3 listed no other drug. A few people seem to be listed twice.
Designer benzos have turned up in fake Xanax pills, and buyers often don't know what's in them.
cl_benzo_designer.rate: Reports of people who got sick or died, with no count of everyone who used. The poison-centre drugs were never lab-checked, and the deaths come from a review of case reports.

lsd.statement: Blotters taken as LSD always hold LSD.
lsd.why: In some reported cases, blotters taken as 'acid' held an NBOMe instead. Nobody has counted how often this happens.

lsd.statement: Published NBOMe cases had far more seizures than poison centre cases.
lsd.why: About 38 in 100 published cases had seizures, against 4 in 100 of 25 cases at Texas poison centres. Published cases are often the worst ones.

benzodiazepines.statement: Most deaths linked to designer benzos involved no other drug.
benzodiazepines.why: In a review of published cases, 115 of 141 death entries also listed an opioid, and only 3 listed no other drug.

benzodiazepines.statement: Designer benzos have been shown to be riskier than prescribed benzos.
benzodiazepines.why: Nobody has compared them. The reports only count people who got into trouble, so they can't say how risky one use is.
